policies.policy_name: Mandatory fields must be provided for add_child_incidents
policies.description: The request must include both the required parameters — parent_incident and child_incidents — before invoking the add_child_incidents tool.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.policy_name: Verify incident identifiers exist before creating relationships
policies.description: Do not assume incident IDs are valid; the parent and each child incident ID must be looked up and confirmed to exist via verified API results before calling add_child_incidents.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results.
When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.

policies.policy_name: User role must have CRUD permissions on incidents
policies.description: Only users with roles that grant full CRUD access to incidents (Administrator, Manager, or Agent) are permitted to create parent‑child incident mappings.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.

Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables. Can update assignment, state, and resolution.

policies.policy_name: Batch endpoint usage is permitted under atomic operation rules
policies.description: add_child_incidents is a batch operation; it may be executed because the policy allows batch endpoints as an exception to the one‑operation‑at‑a‑time rule.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.

policies.description: If a user request violates any rule in the policy document, the assistant must immediately stop the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.
references: Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

policies.description: The assistant must never disclose information that lies outside the authenticated user's access scope when creating or managing parent‑child incident relationships.
references: Knowledge Scope: Do not disclose information that is outside the authenticated user's access scope.

policies.description: When handling a request to add child incidents, the assistant must not ask the user for additional information. If the request is ambiguous or missing mandatory fields, it must return the list of required inputs and state the ambiguity or missing field.
references: User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.

policies.policy_name: Log timestamps and actor for child‑incident mappings
policies.description: Every creation of a parent‑child incident mapping must be recorded with the timestamp (`created_on`) and the `user_id` of the actor performing the operation.
references: Time Tracking: All work logs must include the timestamp (created_on) and the user_id performing the action.
